emergency.title: Something tripped
emergency.subtitle: Answer a couple of questions and we'll work out what to do.

mcb.title: A breaker tripped
mcb.why: A breaker trips on overload (too many powerful appliances on one circuit) or on a short circuit (a faulty appliance or wiring).
steps: Unplug the powerful appliances on this circuit: kettle, heater, iron, hair dryer.
Push the breaker lever up until it clicks.
If it stays on, plug appliances back one at a time, not all at once.
If it trips immediately even with nothing plugged in, it's a short circuit. Leave it off and call an electrician.
If it trips when you switch on one particular appliance, that appliance is faulty.

rcd.title: An RCD tripped
rcd.why: An RCD cuts the circuit when current leaks: moisture, damaged insulation, a faulty appliance. It protects against electric shock, so don't ignore it.
steps: Unplug every appliance on the circuits behind this RCD (listed below).
Push the RCD lever up.
If it holds, switch appliances back on one by one, starting with the suspects: washer, water heater, kettle, anything near water.
The appliance that makes the RCD trip is faulty. Don't use it.
If the RCD trips with everything unplugged, the wiring is the problem. Call an electrician.

relay.title: The voltage relay tripped
relay.why: The relay disconnects the apartment when grid voltage leaves the safe range, protecting your appliances from surges.
steps: Look at the relay display to see the voltage.
Wait: once the voltage is back to normal, the relay restores power by itself, usually within 30 to 60 seconds.
Don't flip other breakers or try to bypass the relay.
If it happens often, tell the building management: the problem is in the building's supply.

all.title: The whole apartment is dark
all.why: Three likely causes: the main breaker tripped, the voltage relay tripped, or the whole building lost power.
steps: Check whether neighbours and the stairwell have light. If not, it's a building outage: call the management company.
Look at the voltage relay. Dashes or blinking digits mean wait, it will turn back on by itself.
If the main breaker is down, unplug powerful appliances and push it up.
If everything in the flat panel is on, check the breaker next to the meter. It is often in the floor box on the landing.
If the main breaker trips again, don't keep trying. Call an electrician.

other.title: This device doesn't usually "trip"
other.why: Looks like the wrong device was picked. Find the lever that is down on a breaker, RCD or RCBO.
steps: Go back and pick the breaker whose lever is down.
If no lever is down, check the voltage relay.

afdd.title: The arc fault device tripped
afdd.why: An AFDD cuts the circuit when the wiring arcs: a loose contact in a socket or box, a damaged cable, a faulty extension lead. It is a fire warning.
steps: Unplug everything on this circuit, especially extension leads and old chargers.
Push the lever back up.
If it holds, plug things back one at a time and watch which one trips it.
If it trips with nothing plugged in, or keeps tripping, leave it off and call an electrician: there is a bad contact somewhere.

fuse.title: A fuse has blown
fuse.why: A fuse link melts on overload or short circuit. It does not reset by itself.
steps: Switch off heavy appliances on this circuit.
Open the holder and take the link out. A blown one has a dark window or an unlit indicator.
Fit a new link of the same rating, printed on its body.
Never fit a higher rating and never replace it with wire.
If the new one blows at once, it is a short circuit. Call an electrician.

emergency.suspects: The most powerful appliances on this circuit

danger.title: Danger: act now
danger.s1: If you can do it safely, switch off the main breaker
danger.s2: Don't touch the panel with wet hands and don't open it if there is smoke.
danger.s3: If there is smoke or fire, leave the apartment and close the door.
danger.s4: Call 112 and report an electrical fire.

emergency.never: Never hold a lever up by hand so it "stays on", and never tape breakers. That disables protection against fire and electric shock.

cable-marginal.title: Breaker at the cable's limit

selectivity-equal.title: Same rating as the upstream device
selectivity-equal.hint: On overload {upstream} may trip instead of this circuit and cut more than needed.

rcd-underrated.title: RCD may lack overload protection
rcd-underrated.hint: A {rating} A RCD sits behind {upstream} rated {upRating} A, and the breakers under it add up to more than its rating.

rcd-cascade.title: RCD behind RCD without selectivity
rcd-cascade.hint: {leakage} mA sits behind {upstream} at {upLeakage} mA. A leak can trip both. Use a selective (S) device of 100 mA or more upstream.

rcd-class.title: Type AC RCD in front of inverter equipment

phase-imbalance.title: Phase imbalance
phase-imbalance.hint: L1 {L1} W · L2 {L2} W · L3 {L3} W. Redistribute the load.

channel-mismatch.title: Channel controls a point on another circuit
channel-mismatch.hint: Channel {channel} is linked to "{point}", but that point isn't fed by this actuator.

ga-unknown.title: Group address leads nowhere
ga-unknown.hint: "{point}" sends to {group}, but no actuator channel listens to it.

route-diagonal.title: The route runs diagonally
route-diagonal.hint: Route {route} has a slanted section. Cables are laid parallel to the walls so the plan shows exactly where they are. Redraw the section horizontally and vertically.

route-off-wall.title: A wall run crosses the room
route-off-wall.hint: Route {route} is set to run in the wall, but part of it is more than 30 cm away from any wall. Keep it along the walls, or switch it to the floor or the ceiling.

route-drop-midair.title: The drop to a point is not in a wall
route-drop-midair.hint: Route {route} rises or drops to "{point}", which is more than 30 cm from a wall. Vertical sections only run inside walls: move the point to a wall or route the cable differently.

conductor-mismatch.title: Conductors swapped on a link
conductor-mismatch.hint: Terminal {terminal} of {device} carries {conductor}, but {to} is marked {other}.

cable.title: Cable size and breaker rating
cable.body: A breaker protects the cable, not the appliance. Copper in walls: 1.5 mm² up to 10 A, 2.5 mm² up to 16 A, 4 mm² up to 25 A, 6 mm² up to 32 A. A larger breaker lets the cable overheat.

load.title: Circuit load
load.body: Current is derived from appliance power with demand factors: sockets 0.3, lights 1, appliances 0.7 to 1. The whole panel also gets an overall factor based on the number of circuits.

selectivity.title: Selectivity
selectivity.body: A downstream breaker must be rated lower than the upstream one, so a fault cuts one circuit rather than the whole apartment.

rcd.title: RCDs and cascades
rcd.body: A 30 mA RCD protects people. Two RCDs in series without selectivity trip together, so the upstream one should be selective (S), rated 100 or 300 mA.

wet.title: Wet zones
wet.body: Everything in bathrooms and toilets must sit behind a 10 or 30 mA RCD or RCBO.

class.title: RCD type
class.body: Washers, dishwashers, induction hobs and inverter ACs produce pulsating leakage currents. They need type A; type AC can't see them.

input.title: Supply capacity
input.body: Estimated demand is compared with the contracted capacity, which you can set in the editor's general settings.

routes.title: How routes are laid
routes.body: Concealed wiring runs only horizontally and vertically, parallel to the walls. A wall run stays in the wall. From the floor or the ceiling, the cable goes down a wall to the socket or switch, never through open air.

smart.title: Smart home
smart.subtitle: Bus devices (KNX and others), their addresses and what controls what.
smart.empty: This panel has no bus devices. If you have KNX, DALI or Modbus, add actuators, a bus power supply and control panels in the editor.
smart.safety: An actuator channel is a relay driven by software. A light switched off from a panel is still live. Switch off the breaker before touching wires.

hero.badge: A QR code on the panel door
hero.title: Scan the panel door to see what each breaker controls
hero.subtitle: A sticker on the door of your electrical panel opens a site with the panel layout and a floor plan of the apartment. It tells you which breaker to switch off before replacing a socket and where the cables run under the plaster. If something trips, a step-by-step guide is right there. The data is encrypted, and after the first visit the site works offline.
hero.live: Points without power on the plan: {n}

describe.title: The electrician fills in the panel
describe.body: Rows of breakers, RCDs, the floor plan with sockets, cable routes and photos of the walls before plastering. The editor runs in the browser, and there is a desktop app too.

encrypt.title: It all ends up in one file
encrypt.body: The .panel file is encrypted with a password. Send it to the owner, or publish it to GitHub Pages straight from the editor.

stick.title: The QR code goes on the door
stick.body: The password is already inside the code, so nobody types it. On the first visit the phone keeps a copy, and after that the site opens without internet.

features.title: What the site shows
features.subtitle: Answers to everyday questions like "what do I switch off to replace this socket", plus the checks an electrician would normally run.

panel.title: A panel that looks real
panel.body: Breakers are drawn to scale with their rating and curve, and RCDs show their residual current. Tap any of them to see what it supplies and how loaded it is.

find.title: What to switch off?
find.body: Pick a socket or the water heater. You get an answer like "row 2, fifth from the left", and the breaker lights up on the panel.

emergency.title: When something trips
emergency.body: A step-by-step guide anyone in the household can follow. It helps work out what happened and when it is time to call an electrician.

plan.title: Where not to drill
plan.body: The floor plan marks sockets, lights and cable routes with a strip where drilling is off limits. You can attach photos of the walls taken before the renovation.

checks.title: Wiring checks
checks.body: The app compares cable sizes with breaker ratings, adds up the load on each circuit and checks selectivity. It also makes sure wet rooms are behind an RCD and inverter appliances get the right RCD type.

schema.title: Single-line diagram
schema.body: Drawn automatically from the panel data. Current flows through it as an animation, and you can switch breakers off to see what goes dark.

smart.title: Smart home and KNX
smart.body: Actuators, group addresses and wall panels in each room, so you can see which channel switches what. The app never treats a smart relay as isolation and points to the breaker in front of it.

labels.title: Labels and QR codes
labels.body: Breaker labels print at true scale. Every device gets its own QR code.

offline.title: Works during a power cut
offline.body: When the main breaker trips, the router goes down with it. A site you have opened once still loads from the phone's storage.

privacy.title: Only people with the password can see your floor plan
privacy.p1: The browser encrypts the data with AES-256-GCM. The key is derived from the password with PBKDF2.
privacy.p2: The host only stores the encrypted file. The site has no server or database of its own.
privacy.p3: The password sits in the link after the # sign. Browsers never send that part of the address to the server.
privacy.p4: Photos and documents are stored in the same encrypted file.
privacy.scan: This QR code opens the demo apartment

diy.title: Make your own
diy.subtitle: Everything happens in the desktop app. All you need is a free GitHub account: no forking, no tokens.
steps: Download the desktop app and open it.
Choose "Create a new panel". If your electrician sent you a .panel file, open that instead.
Fill in the panel and the plan. The app asks for a password the first time you save.
In "Save & publish", press "Sign in with GitHub", then "Create a new site" and "Publish".
Print the labels in "Labels & QR" and stick the QR code on the panel door.
Press TEST on the RCDs once a month. If you forget, the app reminds you.

electrician.title: If you are an electrician
electrician.text: Describe the panel in the app on your side and hand the client the .panel file. They open it in the app and publish the site from their own GitHub account. Yours is not needed.

manual.title: By hand, for developers
manual.text: You can fork the repository, turn on GitHub Pages and publish with a GitHub token, or just replace public/app/panel.enc.json. Details in the README.

landing.footer: The site does not replace a wiring design or an inspection by an electrician.

load.title: Load
load.text: How much the flat can draw at once and whether the allowed supply is enough.

list.title: What is wrong
list.text: Each issue explains the problem and links to the device.

task.title: Schedule
task.text: What to do with the panel and how often: RCD test, terminal re-torque, meter readings.

done.title: Mark as done
done.text: Press it when done; the next due date is worked out for you.

options.title: What to print
options.text: A door sticker, strips for the breakers and a QR code for every device.

sticker.title: QR for the door
sticker.text: This code opens the site straight away, no password to type.

print.title: Printing
print.text: Print at 100% so the strips match the breaker widths.

scenarios.title: What happened?
scenarios.text: Pick the situation and the app walks you through it.

smell.title: If it is dangerous
smell.text: A burning smell, sparks or a hot panel: this button first.

tabs.title: Editor tabs
tabs.text: General, panel, plan, photos, maintenance and publishing.

history.title: Undo and draft
history.text: Every change goes to a draft on this device, and mistakes can be undone.

meta.title: Name and address
meta.text: The site address is used in the QR codes. A site created from the app fills it in.

supply.title: Supply
supply.text: Phases, voltage, allowed power and the account number.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.text: The electrician and the building management. Their numbers show up in "Something tripped".

preview.title: Preview as the client
preview.text: Opens what the panel owner will see on the site in a separate window. It updates by itself while you edit.

tabs.title: Editor tabs
tabs.text: General, panel, plan, photos, maintenance and publishing.

board.title: Add a device
board.text: Press "+" on a free spot of the rail and pick what goes there.

view.title: Panel or list
view.text: The list is handy for row widths and blanks.

addrow.title: Rows
addrow.text: Add a row if the panel has more rails.

aside.title: Properties
aside.text: The selected device is set up here: rating, wiring, maintenance.

modes.title: Tools
modes.text: Room, outline, opening, point, cable and photo. Click the plan to place one.

canvas.title: Plan
canvas.text: Drag to move, scroll to zoom. Type a number to set a wall or cable length.

view3d.title: Check in 3D
view3d.text: Switch over to see heights and runs in space.

aside.title: Properties
aside.text: The selected room, point or run is edited here.

add.title: New task
add.text: Add your own task. Standard ones are suggested on the device card.

task.title: Task and log
task.text: Interval, instructions, devices and the record of when it was done.

file.title: File
file.text: Save an encrypted .panel to hand to the electrician or the owner.

site.title: Site
site.text: Publish the panel to your own site: sign in with GitHub and create one in a couple of clicks.

password.title: Password
password.text: It encrypts the data and cannot be recovered. Write it down.

viewer.emptyHint: The owner of this panel has not put the data on this site yet. Check back later.
viewer.failedHint: Check your connection and try again.
